data.text:
M/S R K Products Company vs The Union Of India on 22 March,
2024
Author: Surepalli Nanda
Bench: Surepalli Nanda
 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda
 Writ Petition No.13208 of 2013
Order: 
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Counsel appearing on behalf of respondents. 
2. The petitioner approached the Court seeking prayer as under:
"...to issue a direction or a writ one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondent in Seizing the consignment containing Sagar Gutka packets under the joint Survey proceedings dt 11-03-2013 as illegal contrary to law and judicial precedents and consequently direct the respondent to release the same and be pleased pass orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit."
3. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondents has filed counter affidavit and in particular, paragraph Nos. 4, 5 and 6 of the said counter affidavit reads as under:
"4. As per the Joint Survey only 80 bags of prohibited pan masala for loading by Train A.P. Express to be transported to Jammu were seized and not as falsely contended by the Petitioner in Para 3 and ground no.1 of the Affidavit.
5. As per the Joint Survey Report, which is marked as Ex. P-1, wherein the material was seized on the midnight of 11/03/2013 by Food SN,J WP_13208_2013 Safety Officer and was temporarily kept at the RPF Post, Secunderabad and thereafter the same was taken by Food Safety Officer and Govt.
Railway Police, who registered and filed the charge sheet under CC NO. 895/2013. 
6. A criminal case was filed by Sub Inspector/Government Railway Police, Secunderabad, a separate wing controlled by the State Authority and the case was filed before concerned Hon'ble Magistrate and numbered as CC No.895/2013 against the owner of the seized Gutka and not the Writ Petitioner. The Accused/Owner of seized goods pleaded guilty and was convicted by the Hon'ble II Metropolitan Magistrate for Railways, Secunderabad vide Judgment dt. 26-9-2013. The copy of the Judgment is enclosed herewith."

1 4. Taking into consideration the specific averments made at paragraph Nos. 4, 5 and 6 of the Counter affidavit filed by the respondents, the writ petition filed by the petitioner is dismissed. 
However, there shall be no order as to costs. 
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
